title: Borneo International Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Edition Was Like
seo_title: Borneo International Marathon 2027 Review | Kota Kinabalu
meta_description: Borneo International Marathon review: the 2026 edition drew more than 10,000 runners, but a car hit a runner on the course. What that means for 16 May 2027.
dek: Sabah's biggest road race put more than 10,000 runners on the roads of Kota Kinabalu on 10 May 2026. Here is what that edition was like, including what went wrong, and what it tells you about entering the 2027 race on 16 May.
verdict: The Borneo International Marathon is the established marathon of East Malaysia: the 2026 edition was its 16th, it drew more than 10,000 runners [1][2], and Filipino runners won both the men's and women's marathons [2][3]. It was also a race with real problems. A car hit a marathon runner and a Rela crew member on the course before dawn [1], the women's half-marathon winner said there were few marshals on a route full of narrow turns [3], and a half-marathon runner later died after having trouble breathing when he finished [1]. If you enter the 2027 race, study the posted route and don't count on marshals being at every turn.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition in Numbers
paragraphs: The 2026 Alliance Bank Borneo International Marathon was run on Sunday 10 May, its 16th edition, and drew more than 10,000 runners [1][2]. It offered three distances: the full marathon, a 21.1 km half marathon and a 10 km [2], based at Likas Sports Complex in Kota Kinabalu [4].

The two reports disagree on the size of the international field. The Star gives runners from over 50 countries [1]; the New Straits Times gives 35 [2]. What neither disputes is that the field was well into five figures.

The New Straits Times reports that the race began at 2am [2]. However the individual flag-offs were staggered, this is a race run almost entirely in the dark, and it is built that way deliberately: finishing before the sun is fully up is the difference between a hard tropical marathon and a dangerous one.

sections.heading: A Filipino Sweep at the Front
paragraphs: Edsel Moral won the men's marathon in 2:38:02, ahead of fellow Filipino Dikyias Mendioro in 2:39:41 and Japan's Shinji Watanabe in 2:41:18 [3]. Lizane Abella led a Filipino sweep of the women's marathon in 3:16:26, from Jennylyn Nobleza in 3:16:33 and Maricar Camacho in 3:17:24 [3].

The half marathons went the same way. Eduard Flores was first home in the men's 21.1 km in 1:11:03 [2], and university runner Asia Paraase won the women's open 21 km in 1:28:35 on her international debut, ahead of Filipina Jamine Cruz and Singapore's Amber Jia Qi Chew [3].

Most of those winners came as one squad: Team 7-Eleven Philippines, a group of 17 qualifiers from that company's Manila race series, sent to Kota Kinabalu for the first time in 13 years [5]. Those winning times are useful as a guide to how fast the course can be run on a humid May night, not as evidence of how deep the local field is.

sections.heading: What It Was Like to Run
paragraphs: The most useful first-hand account of the 2026 course comes from Paraase herself. Speaking to Cebu Daily News, she said the route had many narrow streets that could easily confuse a runner, that there were only a few marshals, and that runners needed to check the posted route to avoid getting lost [3].
She also said the climate was much like home in the Philippines but the air felt heavier, and that this made the race harder. Even so, she called the experience great and very enjoyable [3].

That is one runner's view and it should be read as such, but it is the view of someone who was at the front of the race, where the course is emptiest and wrong turns are easiest to make. If you are travelling in for 2027, walk or drive the tricky sections of the posted route the day before rather than trusting marshals to point the way.

sections.heading: The Hit-and-Run, and a Death After the Finish
paragraphs: Two serious incidents marked the 2026 edition. At about 3.30am, a Proton Saga hit a 42 km runner from behind on Jalan UMS, heading towards Likas, while he was in the left lane that had been set aside for participants [1]. Police said safety cones had been placed along that lane to separate the race from traffic, and that the car kept going before stopping at a traffic light [1]. The runner had light injuries to his hand, knee and neck and was treated at Gleneagles Hospital Kota Kinabalu [1].

The organiser, the Kinabalu Running Club, said a Rela crew member was also hit, and that both received immediate attention from the event's medical team before being taken to hospital [1]. The Star reported that social media users questioned traffic control along the route, and that the authorities had yet to explain how the car got into the race area [1].

Separately, a half-marathon runner, Muhd Irfan Tarmizi Muhlis, a lifeguard, died after having trouble breathing when he finished [1]. The cause has not been given in the reporting cited here, and nothing in it links his death to the organisation of the race. It is a reminder that a tropical race in the small hours is still a hard physical effort, whatever the time on the clock.

sections.heading: What to Expect in 2027
paragraphs: The 2027 race is scheduled for Sunday 16 May 2027 [6], six days later in the calendar than 2026. It is organised by the Kinabalu Running Club [6], which founded the race in 2008, when the first edition drew 529 runners [7].

The 2027 distances, start times and entry fees had not been published when this review was written. Assume a similar pre-dawn schedule to 2026 when you plan the night before, and check the official site for confirmed start times before you book.

The question for 2027 is whether traffic control changes after 2026. Cones along a shared road did not stop a car reaching a runner [1]. Before you enter, look for what the organiser says about road closures on the marathon route.

sections.heading: Should You Enter?
paragraphs: If you want a big-field marathon in East Malaysia, yes. More than 10,000 runners took part in 2026 [1][2], the field draws runners from well beyond Malaysia, and the race has been run by the same club since 2008 [7].

But enter with your eyes open. In 2026 the route was hard to follow in places [3], and at least one section was shared with traffic [1]. Learn the course, run with a light and something reflective on the road sections, and don't assume every turn will be marshalled.

This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2026 edition, including one participant's account given to a newspaper. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Borneo International Marathon in 2026?
faqs.answer: More than 10,000 runners took part in the 16th edition on Sunday 10 May 2026, across the full marathon, the 21.1 km half marathon and the 10 km. Reports differ on how many countries were represented: The Star gives over 50, the New Straits Times 35.

faqs.question: Who won the 2026 Borneo International Marathon?
faqs.answer: Filipino runners won both marathons. Edsel Moral took the men's race in 2:38:02 and Lizane Abella the women's in 3:16:26, with Filipinos filling the women's podium. In the half marathons, Eduard Flores won the men's race in 1:11:03 and Asia Paraase the women's open 21 km in 1:28:35.

faqs.question: What happened at the 2026 Borneo International Marathon?
faqs.answer: At about 3.30am a car hit a 42 km runner from behind on Jalan UMS, in a lane coned off for the race. The organiser said a Rela crew member was also hit. Both were treated in hospital. Separately, a half-marathon runner died after having trouble breathing when he finished.

faqs.question: Is the Borneo International Marathon course closed to traffic?
faqs.answer: Not entirely, on the evidence of 2026. Police said the stretch of Jalan UMS where a car hit a runner had safety cones along the left lane to separate the race from traffic, so the runners shared that road with moving vehicles. Check what the organiser publishes about road closures for the 16 May 2027 race.

editorial_notes: Written about the PREVIOUS edition (10 May 2026), from published reporting on it, to help a reader decide on the next one. The Daily Express and the organiser's own results page could not be read (bot protection, and a 403), so no figure here comes from them. Where the two reports disagree -- 35 countries or over 50 -- both are given. No rating: one participant's quote in a newspaper report is not enough to score an event.
